hero.lead: I'm Hristo — a full-stack developer with 10+ years of experience, working mostly in the frontend with React and TypeScript. I've built and maintained large web applications for clients in banking, air travel, manufacturing and property rental, usually as the senior person the team leans on for the hard parts and the last mile of polish.

work.title: Four projects that show how I work
work.note: Client names stay confidential — most of this ran through a consultancy. Happy to walk through the detail on a call.
work.more: // more detail, screenshots and code walkthroughs available on request

platform.title: One host, seven sub-apps, one shared component library
platform.body: One host application carrying the infrastructure — auth, routing, theming — and seven sub-applications taking their dependencies from it. I helped set this up and kept building inside it.
points: Seven sub-apps on one host, each shipped by its own team without breaking the others
The client-facing app composed from federated widget modules loaded at runtime
A shared component library of atoms, molecules and organisms used by every app
Playwright and Jest coverage plus CI checks that keep independent deploys safe

manufacturing.title: A dashboard per machine, across the whole production line
manufacturing.body: Every machine in the production flow gets its own dashboard, fed live from the floor and read by operators mid-shift. Widgets, data sources and layouts are all configurable, so a new line, plant or customer is setup work rather than a new codebase.
points: One data-source-driven app replaced separate dashboard builds per client
Station-by-station view of the line, plus a drill-down dashboard per machine
Built for the floor: glanceable, high contrast, tolerant of gaps in the data feed
Heavy tables and charts kept fast with ag-Grid and ag-Charts
manufacturing.shot: // schematic line view, not client data

chat.title: A support chat widget small enough to drop into any page
chat.body: A client-facing chat client written in Preact and injected on demand, so the host page pays nothing until a user opens it. It talks to the page through custom HTML events instead of a shared framework, which kept dependencies at zero and the bundle tiny.
points: Preact instead of React, loaded lazily on first interaction
Custom DOM events as the public API — no coupling to the host app's stack
Isolated styling so it can't be broken by whatever CSS the host page ships
chat.shot: // representative UI, not a client screenshot

graph.title: React wrapper around a graph visualisation engine
graph.body: A reusable React layer over a graph rendering engine: nodes and labels authored as ordinary React components, with configurable options and several switchable layout algorithms behind one API.
points: Nodes, edges and labels rendered as React components instead of engine templates
Layout algorithms — hierarchic, organic, radial, tree — swappable at runtime
Configuration-first API so product teams use it without learning the engine

process.title: How a project runs with me, start to finish

steps.title: Communication & planning
steps.body: Understanding what the release actually needs, breaking it down, estimating honestly and agreeing scope with whoever owns the outcome.

steps.title: Setup & structure
steps.body: Project foundations: build tooling (webpack, rsbuild, esbuild), TypeScript and ESLint config, folder and module boundaries, the MUI or design-system layer.

steps.title: Implementation
steps.body: The bulk of the work — complex stateful React interfaces: data grids, dashboards, configurators, long forms, and the polish that makes them feel finished.

steps.title: Testing
steps.body: Playwright end-to-end flows, Jest unit and integration tests, review standards — written as the feature lands, not bolted on before release.

steps.title: Deployment
steps.body: CI/CD pipelines, preview and staging environments, release checks and monitoring after the deploy — plus the handover notes for whoever runs it next.

principles.title: Polish where it pays. Pragmatism everywhere else.

items.title: Detail is the deliverable
items.body: The last 10% — empty states, focus rings, loading behaviour, the pixel that's one off — is what makes software feel expensive. I don't hand over work that needs a second pass.

items.title: But not polish at all costs
items.body: I ask what the release actually needs. Some screens deserve a week; some deserve a day and a note in the backlog. Knowing which is which is most of the job.

items.title: Easy to pick up after me
items.body: I write code, conventions and notes assuming a developer who has never met me will extend it under deadline. Clear structure, no clever tricks that only I can maintain.

items.title: Direct, low-drama communication
items.body: Estimates I stand behind, risks flagged early, no surprises at the demo. I work in English and Bulgarian, remote-first, inside your process and rituals.

engagement.title: Ways we can work together

items.title: Contract via my own company
items.body: Invoiced company to company, hourly or monthly rate. Full-time or part-time capacity, fixed for a quarter or rolling.

items.title: Full-time senior role
items.body: The right product and team is worth joining properly. Remote or hybrid, senior or lead track.

items.title: Setup or clean-up work
items.body: A few weeks to start a greenfield frontend, modernise the build and tooling of an existing one, or review test coverage before you grow the team.

engagement.note: Based in Sofia, Bulgaria — a full working-day overlap with the rest of Europe and a comfortable morning or evening overlap with the US. Registered company, VAT-ready invoicing, standard NDAs and MSAs no problem. Comfortable as the only frontend developer on a product or as one senior among many on a large programme.

final.title: Have a frontend that needs a steady pair of hands?
final.body: Send a paragraph about the product and the team. You'll get an honest read on scope, risk and fit — usually within a day.

about.title: About
about.p1: Senior full-stack developer with over 10 years of professional experience, focused on the frontend. My daily stack is React, TypeScript, ESLint, rsbuild and MUI. I've delivered large web applications for enterprise clients in banking, air travel, manufacturing and property rental — mostly through a consultancy, working directly with client teams.
about.p2: I like the parts of the job other people avoid: heavy data grids, configurable screens, build and tooling setup, flaky tests, the final 10% of polish. Alongside development I've trained and mentored developers, run technical interviews, communicated with customers and organised work for the team. I started programming in high school and haven't stopped since — which means a long list of technologies behind me and no trouble picking up the next one.

tech.label: Also worked with
tech.list: Also worked with: emotion · styled-components · Sass · Less · TanStack · MobX · Yjs · ag-Grid · ag-Charts · ag-Studio · yFiles · Axios · Lodash · Luxon — and jQuery, PHP, C#, Python and VBA earlier on. Whatever the project runs on, I'll get productive in it.
